title: FDIR: Fidelity-Anchored Decompressed Image Restoration for Human and Machine Perception
abstract: arXiv:2608.00111v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Evaluating restored images requires considering pixel fidelity, human perception, and machine preference. However, existing compressed image restoration methods rarely satisfy all three criteria at once. Regression models preserve pixel fidelity but often produce overly smooth results. Conversely, generative models create realistic textures but tend to drift from the ground truth. To address this trade-off, we propose FDIR (Fidelity-Anchored Decompressed Image Restoration), a framework that uses generative priors while preserving strong pixel fidelity. FDIR works in two stages. First, a quality-guided one-step flow model (QO-Flow) adapts a pretrained latent flow backbone with LoRA to generate a structural prior in a single forward pass. translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.00111v2 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：评估恢复后的图像需要同时考虑像素保真度、人类感知和机器偏好。然而，现有的压缩图像恢复方法很少能同时满足这三项标准。回归模型能够保持像素保真度，但往往产生过度平滑的结果；相反，生成模型能够创造逼真的纹理，但往往偏离真实值。为解决这一权衡问题，我们提出了 FDIR（保真度锚定解压缩图像恢复），这是一个在使用生成先验的同时保持强像素保真度的框架。FDIR 分两个阶段工作。第一阶段，一个质量引导的单步流模型（QO-Flow）通过 LoRA 适配预训练的潜在流骨干网络，在单次前向传播中生成结构先验。第二阶段，一个流条件驱动的细节精修网络（FCDR）并不直接输出该生成图像，而是利用它来预测解压缩输入上的像素空间残差。这种设计
tldr: FDIR 提出一种两阶段的解压缩图像恢复框架，通过单步流模型生成结构先验，再由细节精修网络预测像素残差，在使用生成先验的同时保持强像素保真度，兼顾像素保真、人类感知与机器偏好。
en_tdlr: FDIR proposes a two-stage decompressed image restoration framework that generates a structural prior via a one-step flow model and predicts a pixel-space residual through a detail refinement network, achieving strong pixel fidelity while leveraging generative priors to satisfy pixel fidelity, human perception, and machine preference simultaneously.
